page.layout: Two medallion portraits side by side at the top, with their legends around the rims; below them, full-width text in three paragraphs (the first two full width, the third wrapping around a medallion portrait at the left); signature at the foot; running head and page number at the top.

main_text.l: MARIA REG. HISP. PHILIP. II. VX. I.
PHILIP. II VX. II. MARIA REG. HISP.
ISABEL. VX. III. PHIL. II. HISP. REG.
main_text.p: MARIA Regis Hispaniae Philippi uxor prima, Ioānis Re-gis Portugaliae filia, aspectu, ad beneuolentiam conciliandam apto, graui acutoque sermone, in omni actione mirè prudens, intra paucos annos, confecto vitae cursu, ad æternas sedes, id est ad capiendum virtutis & innocentiae suae fructum, euolauit.

MARIA, Regis Hispaniae Philippi uxor secunda, Henrici VIII. Angliae Regis filia, miram prudentiam, & seueritatem in omni vita persecuta, cumque magni motus in Regno excitaretur, virili animo perduelles extinxit, quanquam inter sacras vir-gines educata, animo his cogitationibus exculto, nullam ge-rendi belli partem nouisset, sed nimirum defendenti catholi-cam religionem, Regiamque maiestatem, Deus ipse malorum ultor affuit, Regnumque in summa obedientia conseruauit.

ISABELLA Regis Hispaniae Philip-pi uxor tertia, Henrici secundi Galliae Re-gis filia, læta facie, sic, ut iucunditatē in-tuētibus afferret, dignitate tamen ea quę Reginam deceat: quamdiu vixit, summa & beneuolentia & obseruatia apud omnes adepta, multis naturae, fortunę, animi que bonis instructa, vim tamen fortunę vitare non potuit. Patrem amisit, immatura morte ereptum: nec multo post, edito immaturi temporis infante, incredibili & Philippi Regis & omnium dolore decessit.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits (coins/medals) are illustrations, not text: left a female bust facing front, right a female bust in profile-turned three-quarter view, lower a male bust with a ruff. Legends transcribed from the rims; the rim lettering of the medallions is partly worn, so the abbreviations "VX." and "HISP." in the medallion legends are read with some doubt. Printed text: "Ioānis" has a macron over the a as printed; "iucunditatē" and "intuētibus" carry printed tildes. "VIII." is printed as V111 in the original. No marginal notes on this page.
